title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1973-11-09

ai_review.summary: High‑energy Winterland ’73 show with stellar performances of They Love Each Other, Eyes of the World and Here Comes Sunshine, captured on a soundboard that is generally good but suffers from speed/pitch quirks.
ai_review.review: The November 9 1973 Winterland concert is praised for its tight playing, soaring jams and memorable moments such as a fiery They Love Each Other, an inspired Eyes of the World sequence and a monster Here Comes Sunshine. The SBD source sounds clear overall, though listeners note noticeable speed/pitch errors, occasional mono punches and brief drop‑outs that keep the recording from being pristine.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews rate the performance 5 ★ and highlight numerous standout songs, while the recording is described as good but with consistent technical flaws (pitch issues, mono punches). Weighted combination yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and balanced SBD, but suffers from speed/pitch problems requiring -2.5% correction, occasional mono punches that lose instruments, a few drop‑outs and digi‑static sections.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens solidly but is described as less exciting until mid‑set; second set builds momentum with long jams and multiple climaxes, delivering a consistently enjoyable experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone and solos are repeatedly praised – loopy licks on Eyes of the World, powerful leads throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh receives kudos for his bass thumping, harmonic work and overall tightness in the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is noted for solid rhythm guitar support and occasional standout fills (e.g., on Rider).
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano/organ work is highlighted as ‘great’ especially during Here Comes Sunshine and Me & My Uncle.
